pages.text: Dad went to the boat, leaving his lunch behind. Mom held out the cloth bundle.
They wanted to take Dad his lunch before the boat left. "We have to get there before the boat horn sounds!"
Riri unfolded the cloth and wrapped the lunch again. Lolo put on boots and stamped impatiently. "We need a tight knot." "There is no time for that!"
Riri tied and untied the knot. She added another piece of bread and tied it again.
Toot—the boat horn sounded. Riri's hands froze on the knot.
Lolo snatched the bundle and ran outside. A delicious smell drifted out.
A flock of seagulls circled Lolo, crying loudly. Lolo could not take a single step.
Riri came after Lolo and took bread from the bundle. She flung it onto the sand far away.
The seagulls rushed toward the bread. In that moment, Lolo dashed to the pier.
Dad took the bundle aboard the boat. The knot was so tight that he tugged at it with his teeth, struggling. Below, the two held their bellies and laughed between panting breaths.
